usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/agentmail/v0/inboxes with optional JSON body {username, domain, display_name, client_id} ($2.00 x402 on Base, one-time inbox provisioning). Returns inbox_id = the full email address (e.g. powerfulrule82@agentmail.to).
usage.outputShape: body.inbox_id and body.email (both = the full new address, e.g. "powerfulrule82@agentmail.to"); also body.organization_id, body.pod_id, body.client_id, body.created_at
quirks: This endpoint is Step 1 of 2: it CREATES a managed inbox ($2.00, one-time). It does NOT send email. Sending is a separate endpoint: POST /v0/inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/send ($0.01 per send).
All body fields are optional; omitting username assigns a random one (got 'powerfulrule82@agentmail.to').
inbox_id IS the full email address and doubles as the from-address; URL-encode it (the @) when using it as a path param in the send endpoint.
client_id acts as an idempotency key on create — safe to retry with the same client_id if the $2 payment goes through but the response is lost.

OWNERSHIP GATE: only the wallet that paid the $2 creation can call the send endpoint for that inbox. Wallet identity IS the auth. The send endpoint returns HTTP 403 'Ownership required' (not 402) for inboxes you don't own — payment flow never starts.
$2 is a one-time provisioning cost — create one inbox and reuse the inbox_id across many sends to amortize.
Inbox created during this QA run: powerfulrule82@agentmail.to (owned by the QA master wallet).
usage.guide: AgentMail is a two-step service; this endpoint is Step 1 (Create inbox). POST to https://x402.orth.sh/agentmail/v0/inboxes with an optional JSON body (display_name, username, domain, client_id all optional) and pay the $2.00 x402 charge on Base. Read the new address from body.inbox_id (it equals body.email). This is a one-time $2 provisioning cost — persist and reuse the inbox_id. To actually send mail (Step 2, outward/irreversible), POST to /v0/inboxes/{inbox_id}/messages/send (URL-encode the @) with {to:[...], subject, text} at $0.01 per send; only the wallet that created the inbox may send from it.
